transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

Well, it’s this memorial I’m putting together for my brother. It started as something simple, but it’s gotten a lot bigger than I meant it to. I’ve been spending most days tracking down songs, calling people, planning displays, even thinking about trips for it.

My wife says I’ve pushed everything else aside—the garden, my walking group, just about everything. I guess that’s why I’m here.
Lately, have you been feeling unusually high, euphoric, or on top of the world?

Yeah… I’d say so. Not exactly “happy,” but I get this feeling like I’m lit up, like I’ve got a real purpose. Like if I get this memorial right, the whole town will finally understand my family and what my brother meant.

But then if my wife questions something, or somebody at the senior center slows me down, I can snap pretty quick. So it’s kind of high energy, but irritable too.
Have you been needing much less sleep than usual?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t been keeping close track of it. Some nights I’m up thinking about things, but I don’t know if it’s much less than usual.
Have you been more active than usual, taking on lots of projects or staying unusually busy?

Yes, definitely more active. I can’t seem to just sit in my chair like I used to. I’m up hauling boxes around, making phone calls, rearranging papers, walking from room to room… it’s like my body’s got more steam in it than a man my age ought to have.
Have you felt like you had special abilities or an unusually important role in making this memorial happen?
I don’t know about special abilities. I mean, I do feel like it matters a lot to me, and I’m the one pushing it along. But “special”… I’m not sure I’d put it that way.
Did these changes start after your brother died?
Yes. It started after my brother passed. I’d say it’s been going on about two months now, since I started working on the tribute for him.
Have you been talking more than usual lately?

Yes, I think so. At the senior center meetings, once I start explaining the songs, the quilts, the photos for the memorial, I just keep going. Before I realize it, I’ve talked over a few people, and my pastor has to gently stop me and say, “Aaron, let’s let someone else speak.”
Have your thoughts been racing lately?

Yes. My mind keeps jumping around. I’ll think about a display case, then suddenly I’m thinking I need to take a road trip to find a cousin, then I’m on some verse from an old ballad. It’s hard to slow it down enough to write things out in any kind of order.
When you’re in this energized state, do you feel rested after only a few hours of sleep?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t been keeping track of my sleep that closely. Some nights I’m up later than I mean to be, but I can’t say for sure that I feel rested on just a few hours.
Has this energized state caused serious problems in your day-to-day life?

Yes, it has. I’ve missed my walking group and book club, and I’ve let the garden go. At the senior center I’ve upset some friends because I keep making everything about the memorial display. My wife says our whole day ends up being about calming me down or steering me away from another phone call, trip idea, or argument.
Have you had experiences where you heard or saw things that other people did not?

Yes. Sometimes when I’m at the kitchen table sorting through my brother’s song sheets, I hear his voice like he’s right behind me. He’ll be humming, or telling me which tune should come next. But when I ask, nobody else in the house heard anything.
When you hear your brother’s voice, do you believe he is truly there speaking to you?

When it’s happening, it feels real to me, like he’s right there behind me humming or telling me which song should come next. But then I look around, and nobody else hears it, so… I know that doesn’t quite make sense. Still, in the moment it feels like him speaking to me.
Do you hear your brother’s voice only when you’re falling asleep or waking up?

No, not just then. It can happen when I’m fully awake, like sitting at the kitchen table going through his song sheets. I’ll hear him humming behind me or saying which tune should come next, clear as day, even though nobody else hears it.
Has this high-energy, revved-up state lasted at least a week without letting up?
Yes, it’s been longer than a week. I’d say about two months now, since my brother passed and I started working on his tribute. It hasn’t really let up much.
Have you felt that you were chosen for a special mission or had unusual powers in connection with this memorial?

Yes… I guess I do feel like there’s something special I’m supposed to do with it. Those old ballads my brother kept, they’re not just songs to me. I’m certain there are warnings tucked in the words, meant for me to notice.

My wife says I’m reading too much into it, but I know what I heard in those songs.
